concepts.def: Family vocabulary: les parents (parents), les frères (brothers), les sœurs (sisters), les grands-parents (grandparents), les cousins (cousins).
Relationships — describing how you get on: 'Je m'entends bien avec...' (I get on well with...), 'Je me dispute avec...' (I argue with...).
Marriage and divorce vocabulary: se marier (to get married), divorcer (to divorce), le mariage, le divorce, le PACS.
Verbs with a reflexive pronoun (me, te, se, nous, vous, se): se disputer (to argue), s'entendre (to get on), se fâcher (to get angry).
Adjectives agree in gender and number: 'sympathique/sympathiques', 'beau/belle/beaux/belles', 'gentil/gentille'.
Two forms of 'you': tu (informal singular, friends/family), vous (formal or plural, strangers/teachers).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Topic 1: Home and Abroad — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Topic 1: Home and Abroad brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Topic 1: Home and Abroad.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I get on well with my brother'?
options: Je m'entends bien avec mon frère.
Je m'entend bien avec mon frère.
Je entends bien avec mon frère.
Je m'entendre bien avec mon frère.

mcqs.q: Which form of 'you' should you use when addressing your French teacher?
options: tu
vous
toi
te

mcqs.q: What is the most common informal way to form a yes/no question in French?
options: Always using inversion (Parlez-vous?).
Adding 'pas' at the end.
Silent.
Rising intonation (statement said as a question) or using 'est-ce que'.
As a nasal vowel - the n is not fully pronounced.
Silent.
Like English 'on'.
Adding 'pas' at the end.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I was using my computer when the phone rang' in French?
options: Adding 'pas' at the end.
J'utilisais mon ordinateur quand le téléphone a sonné.
J'utilise mon ordinateur quand le téléphone sonne.
J'ai utilisé mon ordinateur quand le téléphone a sonné.
